newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER SACKED FOR PUNCHING TEAM MATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GOALKEEPER SACKED FOR PUNCHING TEAM MATE.

text.p: Hot-tempered goalkeeper Pascal Olmeta was sacked by his club Lyon on Wednesday for punching a team mate at the end of a French first division match last month.

The 35-year-old Corsican twice punched veteran defender Jean-Luc Sassus, who had to be taken to hospital with concussion, after Lyon lost 1-0 at home to Nantes on December 20 in their last game before the winter recess.
The former Marseille player has so far refused to comment on the incident or the club's decision.
Olmeta's action appeared to be a reaction to the defeat, Nantes scoring the only goal of the match in the dying minutes.
Sassus, 34, not a favourite of coach Bernard Lacombe, has been loaned for six months to second division St Etienne and is hoping for a permanent transfer.
Lyon have also signed goalkeeper Gregory Coupet from St Etienne.
Olmeta and Sassus, the oldest players on Lyon's books, were the only ones left of those recruited between June 1993 and May 1995 by former coach Jean Tigana, now at Monaco and a hard act to follow.
Olmeta played 131 league games for Lyon since joining them from Marseille in 1993 and 474 in total, the record for players still active in France.
He could continue his career in Japan's J.League.
